articles.summary: Bangladesh expressed hope that India would expedite the extradition process for former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, stating that political will is essential alongside legal procedures. This follows Indian high commissioner's remarks that the legal process is ongoing with no set timeframe.

articles.headline: Telangana woman dies in US road accident
articles.summary: A 31-year-old woman from Telangana died in a road accident in Missouri, US, after a truck hit her car late Saturday night. Daram Supriya, returning home from her restaurant, died on the spot, while her friend sustained injuries.

articles.headline: Russian drones hit Indian pharma plant in Ukraine, 1 dead
articles.summary: Six Russian drones struck an Indian pharma plant in Sumy, Ukraine, killing an engineer and largely destroying the facility. Kusum Group co-founder Sanjeev Gupta called it a "targeted attack," part of increasing strikes on pharma and food facilities.

articles.headline: Strikes hit Kyiv; Ukraine, Germany sign $1.5bn aid deal
articles.summary: Ukraine and Germany signed a $1.5 billion deal for weapons and energy sector support as fresh Russian strikes hit Kyiv during Chancellor Friedrich Merz's solidarity visit. Merz condemned the "barbarous attacks on civilian population" as war crimes.

articles.headline: SIR strikes at Constitution's heart: Ex-SC judge Nariman
articles.summary: Former SC judge Justice RF Nariman stated that the special intensive revision (SIR) process, which led to large-scale deletion of names from voter lists, was intrinsically arbitrary and struck at the heart of the Constitution, disenfranchising millions and creating "second-class citizens".

articles.headline: Karnataka sees 40% dip in foodgrains to market
articles.summary: Karnataka faces a 40% decline in foodgrains reaching APMC yards, including a 33% drop in major pulses by September end. This is attributed to severe drought affecting 47 lakh hectares of agriculture, with further losses expected.

articles.headline: Bengaluru struggles to find public play areas
articles.summary: Bengaluru faces a severe shortage of free public playgrounds due to rapid urbanization, with only 2.2 square meters of outdoor space per person against a WHO standard of 9. Many existing playgrounds are poorly maintained or converted, impacting children's physical activity and requiring integrated solutions from citizens, authorities, and schools.

articles.headline: Bengaluru trio crowned world's best cake sculptors
articles.summary: Three Bengaluru artists — Anna Austin, Arati Mirji, and Samie Ramachandran — won 'World's Best Extreme Cake Sculptors' at the International Cake Show Australia 2026. Their edible Jallikattu sculpture, built live in 12 hours under challenging conditions, showcased cultural storytelling and technical precision.

articles.headline: Olympian Nisha Millet reflects on early morning training
articles.summary: Olympian Nisha Millet reflects on her swimming career in Bengaluru, highlighting the enduring routine of early morning training and the city's transformation. She now runs a swimming academy, with her children continuing the legacy, and cherishes Cubbon Park as her favorite city "adda."

articles.headline: Kasturba Road: A walk through Bengaluru’s history
articles.summary: Kasturba Road in Bengaluru offers a walk through history, art, and science, named after Mahatma Gandhi's wife. It features the Government Aquarium, Visvesvaraya Industrial & Technological Museum, Government Museum, and connections to the Karaga festival, showcasing the city's rich past.

articles.headline: Spouse's legal action not 'mental cruelty': Karnataka HC
articles.summary: Karnataka High Court ruled that a spouse initiating genuine legal proceedings for maintenance or partition does not constitute mental cruelty or justify abandonment. The bench directed a husband, who had abandoned his family, to rejoin his wife and fulfill marital obligations.

articles.headline: Bengaluru techie drowns in quarry during trek
articles.summary: Ganesh Anjaneya Vinay, a 30-year-old Bengaluru techie, drowned in a water-filled stone quarry near Jigani during a trek. His body was recovered after a two-day search involving multiple rescue teams. Police have registered an unnatural death report.

articles.headline: UP carpenter killed in food row in Bengaluru
articles.summary: A 22-year-old carpenter from Uttar Pradesh, Amit Kumar, was stabbed to death by a painter in Bengaluru following an argument over poorly cooked food. The accused, Sunil Kumar, has been taken into custody by RR Nagar police.

articles.headline: Private land clears Nallurhalli traffic bottleneck
articles.summary: A persistent traffic bottleneck on Nallurhalli Temple Road in Bengaluru will ease after a private landowner agreed to allow public use of a portion of his property. Whitefield Rising crowdfunded Rs 4 lakh to asphalt the section, addressing a major commuter issue.

articles.headline: Three family members drown in pond
articles.summary: A 60-year-old man and his two grandchildren drowned in a farm pond in Chintamani taluk, Chikkaballapur district. Muninarayanappa entered the water to rescue Yashwin (7) and Prajwal (8) after they fell in. Locals allege lack of protective fencing led to the tragedy.

articles.headline: Race Course Road shut for 60 days in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Race Course Road in Bengaluru will be shut for 60 days from Monday for white-topping work between Maurya Junction and Hare Krishna Road Junction. Traffic diversions are in place for motorists, BMTC, and private buses, impacting movement towards Majestic and Shivananda Junction.

articles.headline: Citizens protest Bengaluru tunnel road projects
articles.summary: Opponents of Bengaluru's proposed tunnel road projects organized a cycle rally to protest potential environmental and urban impacts. Participants highlighted risks to green spaces and waterbodies, demanding public access to the environmental impact assessment.

articles.headline: Bengaluru residents oppose land for milk parlour
articles.summary: Residents of RR Nagar, Bengaluru, protested the reported allocation of part of Balakrishna Ranga Mandira land for a Nandini milk parlour, arguing the site was designated for a park and health center and fearing further commercial encroachment.

articles.headline: Centre must support drought-hit states: Minister
articles.summary: A central assessment team completed a two-day inspection of drought-hit Hassan, Chitradurga, and Davanagere districts in Karnataka, assessing crop losses, fodder shortages, and drinking water crises. State minister KM Shivalingegowda urged the Centre to provide relief, emphasizing its responsibility under the federal system.

articles.headline: 778 Form-7 applications under scanner in Bengaluru
articles.summary: A complaint has been lodged in Bengaluru alleging a conspiracy to disenfranchise genuine voters in Malleswaram assembly constituency. 778 Form-7 applications, seeking deletion of voters, were reportedly filed against residents still living in the area, with BJP/RSS affiliates implicated.

articles.headline: KIADB's `1.6k-cr work hit by lack of annual plans
articles.summary: A CAG audit found that Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (KIADB) operated for five years without annual or long-term development plans, hampering land acquisition and industrial area development. This resulted in 2,720.5 acres remaining unallotted and significant delays in 78 out of 95 development works.

articles.headline: CM urges coastal, Malnad citizens to be entrepreneurs
articles.summary: Chief Minister DK Shivakumar urged coastal and Malnad region citizens to become entrepreneurs in their hometowns, assuring government support through a new tourism policy. He highlighted plans to utilize Karnataka's 327km coastline for tourism and approved land for a Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams temple in Mangaluru.

articles.headline: Push for supermarkets for government staff
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar has directed Mysore Sales International Ltd (MSIL) to submit a feasibility report for establishing supermarkets, similar to military canteens, offering discounted goods to government employees and their families. The initiative could benefit 80 lakh people and create employment.

articles.headline: 30% of Karnataka waterbodies aid groundwater recharge
articles.summary: A Jal Shakti ministry report reveals that nearly 30% of Karnataka's waterbodies are primarily used for groundwater recharge, emphasizing their critical role in the drought-prone state's long-term water security. Conservation and restoration of these rural waterbodies are deemed a priority.

articles.headline: Shivakumar staging 'drama' over Form 7: Vijayendra
articles.summary: State BJP president BY Vijayendra accused Chief Minister DK Shivakumar of "enacting a drama" over the special intensive revision of electoral rolls and the Form 7 controversy. He urged police not to file FIRs against BJP workers, asserting that the law requires action on Form 7 submissions under the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

articles.headline: Fake drug case: Kingpin's Turkiye link exposed
articles.summary: An SIT probe into a fake drugs racket has exposed a Turkiye connection involving alleged kingpin R Prashanth Babu. He reportedly traveled to Turkiye multiple times a year to procure original labels of a New York-based pharmaceutical company, which were then affixed to counterfeit medicines in India.

articles.headline: Many scientists from remote villages: ISRO director
articles.summary: Isro Telemetry, Tracking and Command Network (ISTRAC) director MR Raghavendra pointed out that many successful Indian scientists come from remote villages, stressing that knowledge, hard work, and determination are more crucial than elite backgrounds for aspiring scientists.

articles.headline: Drought damage already done, flowering failed: Official
articles.summary: Karnataka officials state that despite fields appearing green, drought has already caused significant damage, with flowering not occurring, indicating reduced crop production. The state faces a bleak outlook, with 170 out of 217 taluks declared under "severe drought."

articles.headline: Human side of Sept 30: Pilot's family waited anxiously
articles.summary: The family of Captain Smit Machchhar, injured in the flydubai mid-air incident, endured days of fear and uncertainty, struggling to get updates and travel to his hospital in Abu Dhabi. His father highlighted Machchhar's selflessness and determination to overcome adversity.

articles.headline: 22 missing in Kullu since 2011 untraced
articles.summary: In Kullu’s Parvati Valley, 22 out of 116 people reported missing since 2011 remain untraced. Rescue teams face challenges due to lack of tracking systems and drug tourism. Local operators urge registration posts and mandatory guides to enhance safety.

articles.headline: Minister: Complaint against CEC has substance
articles.summary: Kerala Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala ordered a fresh vigilance probe into a 2006 corruption case against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, stating the complaint has "substance." Allegations involve influencing a World Bank road project and seeking illegal gratification as a PWD secretary.

articles.headline: Democracy in peril from illegal voter deletions: Nariman
articles.summary: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman stated that the "malfunctioning" of the Election Commission and the "illegal knocking out" of millions of voters through special intensive revision (SIR) in West Bengal posed a "great peril" to democracy. He called the process intrinsically arbitrary and a negation of the Constitution.

articles.headline: Six Congress workers get bail in vandalism case
articles.summary: Six Congress workers, arrested for allegedly defacing CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s ancestral residence in Agra during a Sept 28 protest, were granted bail by a court. They had painted slogans on the gate and outer walls of the house.

articles.headline: Protesters confront Delhi cops in anti-CEC march
articles.summary: Protesters marching against CEC Gyanesh Kumar on Day 3 in Delhi pushed barricades, climbed vehicles, and confronted police, leading to 120 detentions. Complaints of sexual harassment by police against three women journalists during Saturday's protest are being investigated by the crime branch.

articles.headline: Raj, Uddhav demand SIR scrapping, EVM return
articles.summary: Uddhav Thackeray and Raj Thackeray, in a joint 'Garjana' protest rally, demanded the scrapping of special intensive revisions (SIRs) of electoral rolls, a return to paper ballots, and elections for the CEC post. Uddhav accused CEC Kumar of acting as a "weapon" for BJP.

articles.headline: End of conflict needs diplomacy: EAM Jaishankar
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar emphasized that ending the Russia-Ukraine conflict requires dialogue and diplomacy, stating India is now more actively involved beyond mere advocacy. He also noted the US's repositioning as a "lonelier power" and increased global competition.

articles.headline: MP couple's newborn daughter strangled in hospital
articles.summary: A one-day-old girl, the third daughter of a couple, was allegedly strangled to death inside the special newborn care unit (SNCU) of a district hospital in Ashoknagar, Madhya Pradesh. Police are questioning her mother and grandmother following the post-mortem report confirming murder.

articles.headline: Wheat MSP hike an 'insult', say farmers
articles.summary: Several farmer organizations under Samyukta Kisan Morcha (SKM) rejected the government's new Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for Rabi crops for 2027-28, calling the Rs 25-per-quintal hike for wheat an "insult." They demanded an immediate revision and full freedom for states to offer bonuses.

articles.headline: 22 monkeys shot dead by crop guards in Chhattisgarh
articles.summary: At least 22 monkeys were allegedly shot dead in a village in Chhattisgarh's Bemetara district by crop guards hired to protect fields. The incident triggered outrage, and a joint forest-police probe has been launched into the serious wildlife crime.

articles.headline: Fodder alarm in drought-hit Marathwada
articles.summary: Drought-hit Marathwada faces a severe fodder crisis due to Kharif season crop failure, threatening its livestock. Fodder stocks in several districts are below state average, with Jalna and Beed having only 63 and 65 days' supply respectively, raising concerns for animal health.

articles.headline: Astrologer Ashok Kharat denied bail in rape case
articles.summary: A Nashik court rejected the bail plea of astrologer Ashok Kharat in a sexual assault and black magic case. The decision was based on multiple criminal cases against him, with the court citing potential adverse effects on ongoing trials if bail were granted.

articles.headline: PG medical seats vacant despite capacity expansion
articles.summary: Despite an 11% increase in PG medical seats for 2026-27 (58,468 seats), over 1,000 seats have remained vacant in the last three years. This mismatch stems from specialty preferences, high fees in private/deemed institutions, and lack of adequate infrastructure and training facilities, making effective capacity lower than approved.

articles.headline: NLSIU offers 20 fellowships to bridge legal research funding gap
articles.summary: The National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru, is offering 20 research fellowships to address the funding shortage for legal research in India. The program aims to foster independent, evidence-based scholarship across law reform, judicial analysis, and public institutions.

articles.headline: NIOS bridge course for primary teachers launched
articles.summary: NIOS has introduced a six-month certificate (bridge) course in Primary Teacher Education (PTE) for in-service primary school teachers holding BEd degrees but lacking a DElEd. This ODL-mode course aims to provide required qualifications and deepen professional expertise for 76,000 registered teachers, primarily in MP and UP.

articles.headline: New HDFC Bank CEO to set house in order
articles.summary: Anup Bagchi, new CEO of HDFC Bank, faces the task of setting the bank's house in order after former chairman Rajiv Kumar found leadership, succession, and regulatory issues. His priorities include recapitalizing the brand, strengthening leadership, optimizing the balance sheet, and balancing insurance-sales culture with new regulations.

articles.headline: Banks' credit offtake exceeds deposit growth
articles.summary: Banks' advance growth continued to outstrip deposit growth in Q2FY27, with loan books expanding double-digit across public sector and mid-sized private lenders. Provisional updates show advances growing between 13% and 29% year-on-year, indicating continued pressure to mobilize deposits amidst strong credit demand.

articles.headline: RBI likely to hike rates, ending cut cycle
articles.summary: The RBI is expected to end its rate-cut cycle this week with a 25 basis point repo rate hike, the first since February 2023. This move, driven by sticky inflation and resilient domestic growth, comes despite geopolitical risks and rupee weakness, and will impact bank lending rates.

articles.headline: India near 8% growth, says PMO official
articles.summary: A top PMO official stated that the Indian economy is within striking distance of 8% growth, driven by GST and banking reforms, flexible inflation targeting, digital payments, and fiscal prudence. He emphasized that India's resilience is an outcome of broad, mutually reinforcing reforms.

articles.headline: International ETFs face volatility, high premiums
articles.summary: International ETFs are experiencing sharp volatility and high premiums to NAV due to regulatory limits on overseas investments, preventing fund houses from creating new units to meet demand. Investors buying at steep premiums risk affecting returns even if underlying markets perform well.

articles.headline: Anthropic brings India-based AI processing to enterprises
articles.summary: Anthropic has enabled in-country inference for its Claude AI models for Indian enterprises via Amazon Bedrock, ensuring prompts and responses are processed on servers in India. This addresses data residency requirements for regulated sectors and is expected to rapidly grow adoption across various industries.

articles.headline: EY India chief seeks easier GST refunds, tax credits
articles.summary: EY India chairman Rajiv Memani urged the GST Council to expedite refunds and address issues with accumulating input tax credit, including for services and capital goods. He also called for consolidating multiple audits and decriminalizing offenses to make GST more user-friendly and boost FDI.

articles.headline: Gill highlights India's World Cup shortcomings
articles.summary: Shubman Gill, India's ODI captain, highlighted critical shortcomings ahead of the World Cup, including a fragile pace attack, poor fielding standards with dropped catches, and the need for a capable batter at No. 8. He emphasized the urgency to finalize the team's core combination.

articles.headline: Marijne rebuilt Indian women's hockey for LA Olympics
articles.summary: Coach Sjoerd Marijne and his support staff systematically rebuilt the Indian women's hockey team after a period of rifts and injuries, focusing on fitness and team cohesion. Their efforts ended a 44-year gold medal drought and secured an unprecedented direct ticket to the Los Angeles Olympics.

articles.headline: Alcaraz advances in Japan Open as Shapovalov retires
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz advanced to the semifinals of the Japan Open after Denis Shapovalov retired due to an upper right thigh injury. Alcaraz was leading 7-6 (7/3), 2-1 when his Canadian opponent withdrew.

articles.headline: Sabalenka knocked out of China Open
articles.summary: World No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka was eliminated from the China Open in the third round, suffering a surprise 6-4, 6-3 defeat to 34th-ranked Czech player Nikola Bartunkova.

articles.headline: India U-17 football team draws 1-1 with Myanmar
articles.summary: The India U-17 men's football team fought back from a goal down to draw 1-1 with Myanmar in a friendly match. Dallalmuon Gangte scored a penalty in the 73rd minute to equalize after Aung Myat Thar had opened the scoring for the hosts.

articles.headline: Karnataka girls lose to UP in basketball bronze
articles.summary: Karnataka girls' basketball team suffered a 65-49 defeat against Uttar Pradesh in the bronze medal match of the Sub-Junior National basketball championship in Vijayawada.

articles.headline: Rohit leads JSC to victory in basketball league
articles.summary: Rohit scored 18 points to lead JSC to a narrow 66-61 victory over Beagles BC in the State 'A' Division League basketball championship in Bengaluru.

articles.headline: Japan Asian Games end, Doha takes 2030 baton
articles.summary: Japan concluded the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games, passing the baton to Doha, Qatar, which will host the 2030 Games. Despite logistical challenges, over 350 records were broken, with 40 out of 45 NOCs winning medals, marking a record for Asian Games.

articles.headline: Indian cinema icon Singeetham Srinivasa Rao dies at 95
articles.summary: Legendary filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao, 1931-2026, died aged 95, leaving a seven-decade legacy in Indian cinema. Known for pioneering and groundbreaking films across multiple languages like the no-dialogue 'Pushpaka Vimana' and time-travel epic 'Aditya 369', he pushed storytelling boundaries.

articles.headline: AR Rahman concert mesmerizes Bengaluru audience
articles.summary: AR Rahman returned to Bengaluru after eight years with 'The Wonderment Tour', delivering a musical spectacle. The maestro, joined by a star-studded ensemble, mesmerized a packed crowd with hits spanning Tamil, Hindi, and a Kannada rendition, creating a memorable evening despite minor hiccups.

articles.headline: Film fraternity demands accountability for AI abuse
articles.summary: The film fraternity, including Chiranjeevi and Vijay Deverakonda, condemned an AI-morphed video allegedly targeting actress Janhvi Kapoor, calling it "cruel, shameful and completely unacceptable." They demanded legal action against AI misuse, stressing that a woman's dignity is not content, and urged governments to take strong measures.

articles.headline: Yami Gautam: Refrain from using AI to alter photos
articles.summary: Yami Gautam requested that AI not be used to alter or enhance her public photographs, asking for images to be used in original form. She stressed that altering an individual’s image without knowledge and consent should not be done.

articles.headline: Earthy eating trend gains popularity
articles.summary: "Earthy eating," embracing wholesome, fibre-rich foods like mushrooms, millets, whole grains, cacao, and fermented foods, is trending. This shift redefines "brown" as signaling nourishing dishes with complex flavors and textures, encouraging mindful eating and a connection to natural ingredients.

articles.headline: SRK, Salman, Prabhu Deva praise pilot Machchhar
articles.summary: Shah Rukh Khan, Salman Khan, and Prabhu Deva publicly praised Captain Smit Machchhar for his courage and duty during the flydubai mid-air crisis. Salman said, "Kamaal kar diya pilot ji, hum sab aap ko salute karte hain," while SRK highlighted his bravery in protecting those onboard.

articles.headline: Pay for extra flight space or trust luck?
articles.summary: The option to pay for an extra, neighbour-free seat on flights is being offered, prompting travelers to consider if the comfort is worth the cost. While some value certainty and privacy, others prefer to rely on luck for an empty adjacent seat on long-haul economy journeys.

articles.headline: Tobey Maguire, Jennifer Meyer officially divorced
articles.summary: Tobey Maguire and Jennifer Meyer are officially divorced as of September 21, after separating in 2016 and filing for divorce in 2020. While their marital status is terminated, some financial and other divorce-related matters are still to be determined. They share two children.

articles.headline: Ben Affleck addresses Shakira setup rumor
articles.summary: Ben Affleck addressed rumors of being set up with Shakira, stating romance is not a "big priority" as he focuses on work and his three children. He acknowledged comments by Ana Navarro, who claimed she tried to set him up with Shakira following his split from Jennifer Lopez.

articles.headline: Stray Kids skip 2027 Grammy submissions
articles.summary: Stray Kids have joined BTS in opting out of 2027 Grammy Award submissions, amidst criticism of a new Asian pop category. Their label confirmed the decision, with the group prioritizing fan happiness over awards and rejecting categorization by region or language.

articles.headline: Milan Fashion Week: Fashion gets "real"
articles.summary: Milan Fashion Week Spring-Summer 2027 focused on making clothes wearable and witty, with designers like Prada, Moschino, and Marni offering new reasons to shop. Trends included dreamy denim, exposed bra tops as outfits, skirts as new T-shirts, and an "unhinged fashionista" attitude.

articles.headline: Justice Bhuyan Critiques Mass Voter Exclusion as Intrinsically Arbitrary
articles.summary: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan stated that any exercise leading to the disenfranchisement of millions is arbitrary and strikes at the heart of the Constitution. Speaking at NALSAR, he emphasized that the right to vote is a constitutional right integral to citizenship. His remarks come amid controversy over the Election Commission's special intensive revision of electoral rolls.

articles.headline: Keralam Orders Inquiry Against CEC Over 2006 Road Project Case
articles.summary: Keralam home minister Ramesh Chennithala ordered a Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau inquiry against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. The probe concerns alleged irregularities in a 2006 road project and the suicide of a Malaysian engineer during Kumar's tenure as state PWD secretary. The inquiry follows a complaint from a Congress leader regarding demands for money to clear project bills.

articles.headline: Iran Insists No Military Solution Exists for West Asia Conflict
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that military confrontation will not solve the conflict with the United States. He warned that any military path chosen by enemies would meet a stronger response. Araghchi called for negotiations based on justice and fairness while the US dials back military operations in favor of economic pressure following heavy initial bombardments.

articles.headline: India Finishes Asian Games With 85 Medals in Aichi-Nagoya
articles.summary: India concluded the Asian Games in Japan with 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver, and 37 bronze. This represents India’s second-best ever tally. Notable achievements included history-making performances in golf, trap shooting, and archery, alongside a double gold in hockey for both men's and women's teams. India won medals across 22 different events for the first time.

articles.headline: UAE Shared flydubai Passenger List With Israel Before Pilot Attack
articles.summary: Emirati authorities reportedly shared passenger and crew details with Israel before a flydubai pilot attempted to crash a flight. The Omani co-pilot, who had been barred from flying in his own country due to extremist views, attacked the captain with an axe. Regional officials revealed that Israel had not raised any red flags on the crew despite receiving their nationalities beforehand.

articles.headline: West Bengal to Bring Laws Against 'Love and Land Jihad'
articles.summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that the state government will implement stringent laws against 'love jihad' and 'land jihad' within six months. Speaking at a VHP event, he also stated plans to implement a Uniform Civil Code similar to Uttarakhand and Gujarat. Adhikari emphasized that the government would not tolerate anti-national activities or attacks on culture.

articles.headline: Donald Trump Taps Jay Clayton to Lead New US AI Task Force
articles.summary: President Donald Trump has appointed Jay Clayton to lead a new government task force on artificial intelligence, dubbed the 'Super Intelligence Force.' The initiative follows a voluntary accord signed by top AI executives to self-police the technology's development. The task force aims to ensure the US leads globally in AI while protecting American interests and improving lives.

articles.headline: Naidu and Chouhan Launch 300,000 PMAY-G Houses in Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh CM N. Chandrababu Naidu and Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan laid foundations for 300,000 welfare houses under PMAY-G 2.0. A first-of-its-kind project in Guntur will use 3D printing technology. Naidu emphasized a goal of 100% housing by 2029 and noted that the Union government increased the state's allocation following a special request for more units.

articles.headline: Kim Jong Un Oversees Launch of AI-Guided Hypersonic Missile
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un supervised the test of a strategic missile capable of changing flight orbits at low altitudes using AI. The missile flew over 700 kilometers after launching from Wonsan. State media reported the drill demonstrated the professional qualifications and counterattack posture of North Korea's strategic missile forces.

articles.headline: RBI Expected to Raise Interest Rates Amid Rising Inflation Risks
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is anticipated to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% this week. Economists predict the Monetary Policy Committee will act to counter rising global commodity prices and headline inflation, which reached a 22-month high in August. This would mark the first rate hike since February 2023, as GDP growth remains stronger than initially forecast.

articles.headline: Tata’s Assam Chip Unit Secures Non-China Suppliers to Mitigate Risk
articles.summary: Tata Electronics has partnered with at least nine technology suppliers from Singapore, Japan, and the Netherlands for its upcoming semiconductor facility in Assam. The strategy aims to reduce dependence on Chinese supply chains and protect the project from geopolitical trade shocks. The facility, costing ₹27,000 crore, is slated to begin production in December.

articles.headline: Mental health concerns widespread among young adults globally
articles.summary: World Mental Health Day (Oct 10) highlights growing mental health concerns, especially among young people. A 2025 global survey found 41% of 18-34-year-olds distressed, compared to 12% of those 55+. In India, 43% of 18-34-year-olds reported struggling. India ranked 8th among G20 countries for this age group.

articles.headline: Govt raises deepwater natural gas price ceiling
articles.summary: The government increased the ceiling price for natural gas from difficult fields (e.g., KG-D6 block) to $9.89/mbtu for October 2026-March 2027, up from $8.90. The ceiling for gas from legacy fields remains $7/mbtu. This could provide relief to producers developing challenging offshore gas resources, while difficult areas retain pricing freedom subject to the ceiling.

articles.headline: India, Canada to begin 5th round of trade talks
articles.summary: India and Canada will start their fifth round of Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) negotiations in Ottawa on October 5, aiming to conclude by year-end. Canadian Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu will visit Delhi later this month. Talks are at a faster pace as PM Modi is expected to visit Canada in December.

articles.headline: India eyeing Ukraine solution: Jaishankar
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar publicly acknowledged India's stepped-up efforts for a Ukraine conflict resolution, engaging with both Kyiv and Moscow. PM Modi has "good ideas," according to Russian President Putin. India focuses on ensuring Black Sea shipping safety, grain exports, and energy supplies. Ukraine received ceasefire proposals from India and three other nations.

articles.headline: FSSAI orders Everest cumin powder recall after safety tests
articles.summary: The FSSAI directed Everest Food Products to recall 'pre-packed cumin powder' after tests found it unsafe due to pesticide residues (Azoxystrobin and Thiamethoxam) exceeding maximum limits. FSSAI also suspended the license of Creative Bakers and Confectioners due to severe hygiene deficiencies, emphasizing strict regulatory compliance for consumer health.

articles.headline: RBI likely to raise repo rate by 25 basis points this week
articles.summary: A Business Line poll of 10 economists suggests the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee will raise the repo rate by 25 basis points this week to 6.75% to tame inflation. Most expect a neutral policy stance.

articles.headline: Softbank CEO warns of AI safety risks
articles.summary: SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son warned about AI safety, stating that exponential surges in AI capabilities necessitate international cooperation and trust to control the greater threat posed by powerful AI models, as machines quickly gain abilities.

articles.headline: Rohini bar to boycott work over alleged lawyer assault
articles.summary: The Rohini Court Bar Association called for a work boycott on Monday after an advocate was allegedly manhandled and assaulted at a police station on September 29. They claim a case was registered against the advocate instead of the police, and senior officers withheld information.

articles.headline: Three women journalists allege sexual harassment by ACP
articles.summary: Delhi Police transferred three complaints to the Crime Branch regarding sexual harassment allegations against ACP Vivek Bhagat by women journalists covering a protest. One journalist alleged molestation. Two others had made similar past allegations, now refiled. Police initially claimed no evidence.

articles.headline: Kuki man found dead in Manipur after abduction
articles.summary: A 71-year-old Kuki man was found dead on Sunday in Manipur, a day after armed men allegedly abducted him at gunpoint and torched his house in Kangpokpi district. Locals suspect Naga extremist involvement. The incident adds to the ongoing ethnic conflict, which claimed over 300 lives.

articles.headline: Djokovic beats Zverev in China Open quarterfinals
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic defeated top seed Alexander Zverev 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 in the China Open quarterfinals, maintaining his unbeaten streak in Beijing. He will face Daniil Medvedev in the semifinals.

articles.headline: Verstappen wins chaotic Bahrain Grand Prix
articles.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, his first win of the season, after a chaotic rain-affected race. He took the lead after an early safety car and led Mercedes drivers Antonelli and Hamilton to the podium.

articles.headline: Merz announces new aid for Ukraine during Kyiv visit
articles.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced a new aid package for Ukraine worth over $1.5 billion during a Kyiv visit, amidst escalated Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities. The package includes $1.1 billion in military aid and $395 million in energy aid.

articles.headline: Brazilians vote in tight presidential election
articles.summary: Brazilians queued to vote in a tight presidential election between Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro. Polls suggested Lula would lead, but not avoid a runoff, with Bolsonaro confident of a first-round win.

articles.headline: RBI hints at cautious approach to interest rate cuts
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) indicated a careful stance on reducing interest rates. Governor Shaktikanta Das suggested that while inflation is moderating, the central bank will closely monitor economic indicators before making significant policy adjustments.

articles.headline: Startup funding sees slight dip in Q2
articles.summary: Venture capital funding for Indian startups witnessed a marginal decline in the second quarter of the fiscal year. While overall investment remains substantial, there's a noticeable shift towards later-stage funding rounds and specific sectors.

articles.headline: New water conservation project launched in Rajasthan
articles.summary: A large-scale water conservation project has been initiated in rural Rajasthan, aiming to improve water availability for agriculture and domestic use. The project involves rainwater harvesting structures and watershed management.

articles.headline: Supreme Court hears plea on environmental protection
articles.summary: The Supreme Court is hearing a significant case concerning environmental protection and the impact of industrial development. The court is deliberating on stringent regulations to safeguard ecological balance.

articles.headline: Metro expansion project progresses in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Work on the metro expansion project in Bengaluru is moving forward as planned. Key construction milestones have been achieved, with an aim to improve public transportation and reduce traffic congestion.

articles.headline: International trade talks resume
articles.summary: Negotiations on a new international trade agreement have resumed between major economic blocs. Discussions aim to address trade barriers and promote global economic stability.

articles.headline: Film festival showcases independent cinema
articles.summary: A prominent film festival has commenced, featuring a diverse selection of independent cinema from across the globe. The festival aims to promote new cinematic voices and storytelling.

articles.headline: Global inflation concerns persist
articles.summary: Despite some easing, global inflation remains a significant concern for many economies. Central banks are weighing the impact of commodity prices and supply chain disruptions.

articles.headline: New pedagogical approach adopted by schools
articles.summary: Several schools across the country are adopting a new pedagogical approach focusing on experiential learning and student-centric methods. The aim is to make education more engaging and effective.

articles.headline: Archaeological team unearths ancient artifacts
articles.summary: An archaeological team has made significant discoveries of ancient artifacts at a historical site. The findings shed light on past civilizations and their cultural practices.

articles.headline: Airport expansion project faces delays
articles.summary: The expansion project at a major international airport is experiencing delays due to logistical challenges and regulatory hurdles. Authorities are working to expedite the process.

articles.headline: Inflation figures show signs of cooling
articles.summary: Latest inflation figures indicate a further cooling trend in the economy. Analysts suggest this could provide room for monetary policy easing in the near future.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh government partners for renewable energy
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government has signed agreements with international firms to boost renewable energy production. The focus is on solar and wind power projects.

articles.headline: Supreme Court panel to review judicial appointments
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has constituted a panel to review the process of judicial appointments. The move follows discussions about transparency and efficiency in the selection of judges.

articles.headline: WHO warns about rise in vector-borne diseases
articles.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued a warning about the rising incidence of vector-borne diseases globally. It emphasizes the need for robust public health interventions.

articles.headline: Renewable energy targets exceeded
articles.summary: The country has exceeded its renewable energy targets for the year, driven by rapid expansion of solar power capacity. This marks a significant achievement in climate action.

articles.headline: Government announces new agricultural reforms
articles.summary: The government has announced a package of new agricultural reforms aimed at boosting farmer income and modernizing farming practices. Key measures include access to technology and markets.

articles.headline: Athletics championship sees new records
articles.summary: A national athletics championship has concluded, marked by several new record-breaking performances. Athletes showcased peak physical condition and competitive spirit.

articles.headline: Quantum computing breakthrough reported
articles.summary: Scientists have reported a significant breakthrough in quantum computing, demonstrating enhanced qubit stability and entanglement. This could pave the way for more powerful quantum computers.

articles.headline: Global economic growth expected to moderate
articles.summary: Global economic growth is expected to moderate in the coming year, according to forecasts from international financial institutions. Risks from inflation and geopolitical tensions persist.

articles.headline: Tennis star withdraws from tournament
articles.summary: A prominent tennis star has withdrawn from the ongoing championship due to an injury. This development impacts the competitive landscape of the tournament.

articles.headline: New vocational training centers inaugurated
articles.summary: Several new vocational training centers have been inaugurated to provide specialized skills to youth. The initiative aims to enhance employability and bridge the skill gap.

articles.headline: Gujarat announces new policies for MSMEs
articles.summary: The Gujarat government has announced a set of new policies aimed at supporting Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). The initiatives focus on ease of doing business and access to credit.

articles.headline: Conservation efforts for endangered wetlands announced
articles.summary: New conservation initiatives have been announced to protect endangered wetlands across the country. The projects aim to preserve biodiversity and ecological balance.

articles.headline: Edtech company secures Series C funding
articles.summary: A prominent edtech company has successfully raised Series C funding, enabling further expansion and product development. The investment reflects confidence in the online education market.

articles.headline: Cricket team secures series victory
articles.summary: The national cricket team has secured a significant series victory against a strong opponent. The team displayed excellent performance throughout the matches.

articles.headline: Dance festival celebrates global traditions
articles.summary: A global dance festival is underway, featuring diverse dance forms and traditions from around the world. The event promotes cultural exchange.

articles.headline: Supreme Court to hear review petition on environmental law
articles.summary: The Supreme Court will hear a review petition concerning a landmark environmental law. The case could influence future ecological protection measures.

articles.headline: UAE shared pilot names with Israel before flydubai incident
articles.summary: UAE authorities reportedly shared pilot names and nationalities with Israel ahead of a flydubai flight where the co-pilot attempted to crash the plane. This raises questions about how the attacker evaded detection, though Israel stated no red flags were raised on the list.

articles.headline: RoI win Irani Cup; Mukesh, Akash star
articles.summary: Rest of India (RoI) defeated Jammu & Kashmir (J&K) by 167 runs to win the Irani Cup for the 33rd time. Pacers Mukesh Kumar (6/33) and Akash Deep (3/25) dismantled J&K's batting lineup, with Ravichandran Smaran's century proving decisive for RoI.

articles.headline: AIFF elections set for December 20
articles.summary: The All India Football Federation (AIFF) decided to hold its much-awaited elections on December 20, ending uncertainty over the timing for electing new office-bearers and the executive committee. The decision was made at a Special General Body Meeting in Kolkata.

articles.headline: Spain beats Czechia; England outclasses Croatia in Nations League
articles.summary: World Cup winner Spain secured a 3-1 victory over Czechia in the Nations League, with goals from Lamine Yamal, Rodri, and Mikel Merino. England overwhelmed Croatia 7-0, with Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka each scoring twice. Spain leads Group 3, England is second.

articles.headline: Outsider Buddy wins Deccan Derby upset
articles.summary: The 30-to-1 outsider Buddy, ridden by Mukesh Kumar, pulled off a major upset by winning the Deccan Derby (Gr. 1) at the Hyderabad Monsoon Races. Trainer Magan Singh Parmar's ward dictated the pace and comfortably held off late challenges.

articles.headline: Australia probes flydubai co-pilot's radicalization links
articles.summary: Australian authorities are investigating whether Hamam al-Hammami, the Omani co-pilot who attempted to crash a flydubai flight, was radicalized during his time studying in Australia between 2015-2017. His student visa was cancelled in 2019 due to non-enrollment.

articles.headline: SC revives LOC against parents in child abduction case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court revived a 'Look Out Circular' against the parents of a man who deceitfully took his three-and-a-half-year-old daughter to the US without informing his wife and refused to return her. The court gave him four weeks to bring the child back or his parents would face legal consequences.
